sentences.english: The book is carried by the boy.
The teacher gives the boy a book.

sentences.latin: Rex filiae suae coronam pulchram dat.
sentences.english: The king gives his own daughter a beautiful crown.

sentences.latin: Urbs magna a militibus fortibus custoditur.
sentences.english: The great city is guarded by brave soldiers.

sentences.latin: Nauta amico fideli donum pulchrum mittit.
sentences.english: The sailor sends the faithful friend a beautiful gift.

sentences.latin: Gladius longus militis a duce sapienti laudatur.
sentences.english: The soldier's long sword is praised by the wise general.

sentences.latin: Femina fratri suo verba dulcia scribit.
sentences.english: The woman writes her own brother sweet words.

sentences.latin: Miles fortis gladium longum et scutum grave portat.
sentences.english: The brave soldier carries a long sword and a heavy shield.

sentences.latin: Oppidum parvum a militibus fortibus et centurione fideli custoditur.
sentences.english: The small town is guarded by brave soldiers and a loyal centurion.

sentences.latin: Dux legionis milites fortes ad proelium magnum ducit.
sentences.english: The general of the legion leads the brave soldiers to the great battle.

sentences.latin: Vexillum legionis a centurione forti et milite fideli portatur.
sentences.english: The legion's standard is carried by a strong centurion and a loyal soldier.

sentences.latin: Imperator clarus victoriam magnam contra gladiatores fortes quaerit.
sentences.english: The famous emperor seeks a great victory against the brave gladiators.
